authenticity_review: The image suffers from severe structural artifacts that undermine photorealism. The most critical defect is the fusion between the mushroom stem and elephant's head—there is no clean contact boundary, realistic shadow separation, or physical plausibility; textures blend unnaturally at the junction. The physics are implausible (massive stone structure balancing precariously on an animal's skull). While individual textures (elephant skin wrinkles, stone granularity) are high-quality, the integration fails basic realism. Additionally, the elephant displays African morphology (large fan-shaped ears, long curved tusks) contradicting the Indian elephant taxonomy provided, though this is a semantic rather than visual artifact issue. The mushroom lacks all biological features (gills, fleshy texture) due to stone rendering—which satisfies the prompt but violates the mushroom class definition.
key_defects: Spatial relationship failure: Mushroom positioned ON TOP of/fused with elephant instead of BEHIND it (critical prompt violation)
Fusion artifact: Mushroom stem melts into elephant's forehead without clean boundary or realistic contact shadow
Taxonomy mismatch: Elephant exhibits African characteristics (large ears, long tusks) despite Indian elephant (Elephas maximus) taxonomy specification
Mushroom biological feature absence: No gills, fleshy texture, or moist appearance due to stone rendering (prompt-compliant but class-inconsistent)
